The cap is a hardcoded module constant with no override in any spelling — not env (`grep -ran 'STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP' packages apps` → 0, and no NESSY_-prefixed equivalent) and not settings (no config key): `const MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HOOK_BLOCKS = 8;` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:136). It is live, not dormant: `base-agent.ts:564` suppresses further feedback once the streak exceeds it, on the Stop path fed by `pi-agent.ts:7312`, and the same streak sources `stop_hook_active` at `pi-agent.ts:7300`.

Three refinements the finding as filed understates or gets slightly wrong:
(a) Parity is a three-part knob, not just "raise the number". `env-vars.md:336` also specifies `0` = disable the cap entirely, and scopes it to **Stop AND SubagentStop**. Our streak map has production call sites only for `Stop` and `ConfigChange` (`pi-agent.ts:7312`, `:7340`) — no `SubagentStop` caller was found, so that half of the documented knob has no counterpart counter to configure at all.
(b) Off-by-one: `streak > MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HOOK_BLOCKS` suppresses on the 9th consecutive block; the doc overrides "after 8". Small, but it means an env override would also need the comparison fixed to land on the documented number.
(c) The gap is already registered as an open deviation at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-hook-context-injection.md:328` and counted in the hooks-guide row of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:85`.
